title: Connected-graph expansion of arbitrary formal weighted double Hurwitz n-point functions from Orlov–Scherbin partition functions
source_title: Explicit closed algebraic formulas for Orlov–Scherbin $n$-point functions
author: Boris Bychkov; Petr Dunin-Barkowski; Maxim Kazarian; Sergey Shadrin
difficulty_reason: The final connected-graph selection is formal once the disconnected expectation is supplied, so it is not the difficulty evidence by itself. Sections2–3 construct the weight-dependent conjugated Heisenberg operators and evaluate their vacuum expectations in the infinite-matrix realization, producing the operator and edge weights used in Proposition3.6. Those new computations and formal-sector coefficient controls remain required after standard Fock-space foundations are allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition3.6, equation27 and its genus/coefficient interpretation28, for arbitrary formal zero-constant psi and y and n>=1. Completed Section3 including full normal ordering and phi_m conjugation10–16 read; raw Schur partition function3 and connected/disconnected definitions4–5 retained. Ordered Laurent sector |z1|<<...<<|zn|<<1 is essential; only positive powers survive the U-plus operator. Previously published boson–fermion/infinite-matrix projective representation and diagonal Schur eigenvalues are explicit research foundations. Complete new vacuum-to-exponential graph weights and connected-cumulant extraction supplied, not the elementary graph inclusion-exclusion identity as a separate problem. No finite-polynomial spectral-curve mainTheorem5.3, topological recursion claim or parameter-specialized Hurwitz family counted. No rationality/convergence assumption imposed on formal series.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The substantive construction conjugates Heisenberg operators by the content-product diagonal operator, evaluates vacuum expectations in the infinite-matrix representation, and transports cumulants to connected graph weights. The resulting formal all-genus weighted Hurwitz formula retains nontrivial coefficient extraction and formal-sector control beyond ordinary qualifying exercises.
